reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
name: Lansky Play-Performance Scale

version.label: Lansky et al. (1987), 0–100 in steps of 10
version.detail: Parent-rated play-performance for children; KPS is used from about age 16.

purpose: Describes functional performance in children with cancer.
intendedPopulation: Children (about 1–16 years), commonly in paediatric neuro-oncology.

options.label: 90: Minor restrictions in strenuous physical activity
70: Greater restriction of play and less time spent in play
60: Up and around, but active play minimal; keeps busy with quieter activities
50: Lies around much of the day; no active play; takes part in quiet play
40: Mainly in bed; participates in quiet activities
30: Bedbound; needs assistance even for quiet play
20: Sleeps often; play limited to very passive activities
10: Does not play; does not get out of bed

resultStates.label: Fully active
resultStates.summary: Fully active, normal play at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Describes play and activity, not the underlying disease.

resultStates.label: Lansky {total}
resultStates.summary: Up and about with reduced play.

clinicalContext.text: The paediatric counterpart of the Karnofsky score, used for trial eligibility and monitoring.

clinicalInsights.text: Usually rated by a parent; record who rated it.

limitations.text: Parent-reported; varies with the child's mood and setting.

limitations: Validated in childhood cancer; less established in other conditions.

guideSections.whenToUse: Children with cancer, including brain tumours.
guideSections.howToPerform: Ask the parent about play and activity over the past week; choose the level.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Used alongside clinical and imaging assessment.

sources.citation: Lansky SB, List MA, Lansky LL, Ritter-Sterr C, Miller DR. The measurement of performance in childhood cancer patients. Cancer. 1987;60(7):1651-1656.
